reformulation: Exact reduction plus binary-design strengthening of cost266-UUE: source 4,161 vars / 1,446 rows (1,332 E, 57 L, 57 G; 12,312 nnz) -> target 4,161 vars / 1,447 rows (1,296 E, 57 L, 94 G; 12,286 nnz). 36 balance equalities are dropped (each equals minus the sum of the other 36 rows of its block, RHS included) and 37 node design cuts are added. Every column, bound, integrality designation and objective coefficient is kept; only the NAME field and the row set change. The integer feasible set and objective are preserved, and the target LP is strictly stronger, proved by a complete 4,161-coordinate rational source point that violates 17 of the added rows.
claim_class: Three claims, no bijection: forward source->target and reverse target->source in integer mode (full 4,161-pair identity projection, objective 'Equal', inverse pointing at the other claim) plus one reverse LP claim (input/output_integers false, inverse null) whose strictness is witnessed by a separating point bound to inclusion_claim 2; two further complete points (Feasible target=false/true, integers=true) check both written models.
claims: Claims 0/1/2 in cases/test44/request.json: {reverse,input_integers,output_integers,objective:'Equal',projection:4,161 pairs,inverse} = (false,true,true,1), (true,true,true,0), (true,false,false,null); the projection is the identity on every kept column and inverse is positional (cases/test44/request.json).

Obligation census by claim 14,273 / 14,272 / 9,940 (preparation.json counts.obligations_by_claim). Claim 0: 4,161 VarLower + 171 VarUpper + 8,494 'Exact' (1 objective + 4,161 projection + 4,161 inverse + 171 integrality) + 1,296 RowEq + 57 RowUpper + 57 RowLower + 37 Local (the 37 cut derivations).

Claim 1 (reverse, integer): the same censuses over 1,446 source rows - 36 of them return as Local Lin facts, each Lin being a -1 combination of the other 36 rows of its block (tools/prepare_test44.py:94). Claim 2 (reverse, LP) drops all integrality references: 4,161 VarLower + 171 VarUpper + 4,162 'Exact' + 1,296 RowEq + 57 RowUpper + 57 RowLower + 36 Local = 9,940.

Points: Strictness{inclusion_claim:2} carrying the complete 4,161-coordinate source point, plus Feasible{target:false,integers:true,objective:null} and Feasible{target:true,...} integer points (tools/prepare_test44.py:114-117); kernel statistics.bijections 0, points 3.

Claim identity is positional only: the check lists are unlabelled sequences, so the recorded negative check breaks a 'middle' obligation by deleting index 2,100 of block 1's Return checks (tools/prepare_test44.py:130).
proof_encoding: 'RPA 3\n' + one compact JSON object {claims,blocks,points} = 3,300,668 B: claims 143,470 B, blocks 3,041,534 B, points 115,622 B (cases/test44/proof.rpa).

Block 0 (forward, integer) has just 74 top-level steps (37 Lin + 37 Cases) yet 2,372,342 B of body: the 37 Cases subtrees carry the nested expansion - 1,746 Cases / 3,638 Lin / 5,238 EqPair steps in total, max Cases nesting 15, and 3,492 branch ends (788 Absurd + 2,704 Witness).

Blocks 1 and 2 (reverse, integer and LP) are 36 Lin steps of the removed-row identity plus a 4,161-entry Return map and check list: bodies 351,924 B and 317,268 B; block 2 carries no integrality references.

Checks are plain positional strings mixing bare 'Exact' with typed refs {VarLower,VarUpper,RowEq,RowUpper,RowLower,Local}; the same claims JSON is written twice - inside proof.rpa and indented as cases/test44/request.json (643,330 B, of which the compact claim content is 143,470 B).

Kernel view (preparation.json kernel_runs[3]): obligations 38,485, branches 1,746, linear_terms 73,109, substitution_terms 57,715, point_coefficient_terms 48,883, peak_live_facts 89, work 1,146,726; execute_us 165,112.
agent_manual_work: Wrote two independent standard-library MPS readers with fractions.Fraction and full section/marker/bound validation (digest evals 'Parsing exact MPS representation', 'Independently auditing generated MPS'); the first attempt died on a SyntaxError at line 65 of the cell, the run's single failing tool call.

Established structure by incidence scans rather than names: union-find over each continuous column's +1/-1 balance pair gave 36 blocks of 37 rows with zero RHS sum and exactly one positive entry; a full 57-edge bridge test, an exact row-signature duplicate test and a row-variable component count followed (digest evals 'Checking full incidence components', 'Verifying common topology and cuts').

Derived the 37 cuts by exhaustive local enumeration: D_n = sum_k abs(b_kn), T_n = smallest attainable sum of degree-many choices in {0,1,4,16} with 7,560*T >= D_n, coefficients min(w,T_n), plus the two largest-option rows for the degree-2 nodes whose demand exceeds 2*30,240; 5,968 local design states enumerated with zero violations (digest eval 'Proving discrete node capacity cuts').

Built the separating witness without any optimisation: each block's demand split equally over all simple directed paths of at most minimum-hop+2 arcs with Birmingham forbidden as transit (up to 110 paths per pair) gave max link load 118,107.02 <= 120,960 and Birmingham largest-option sum 40303/60480; the shorter-path variants that broke capacities L3/L15 were rejected (digest evals 'Constructing explicit relaxation witness', 'Checking bounded simple-path construction').

Wrote output/reformulated.mps with exact finite decimals (decimal_exact), then re-read the artifact with the independent reader, reconstructed all 36 deleted rows from the artifact, re-evaluated 1,446 rows / 4,161 bounds on the witness, and exercised an integer point and an antiparallel circulation counterexample (digest evals 'Writing single committed reformulation', 'Independently auditing generated MPS', 'Exercising written formulation behavior').
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test44.py is 138 lines (811 with its dependencies) and imports parse_mps/row_ref (tools/prepare_affine.py:20,77), expression/plus/mul/expr_json/row_fact/substitute/sha (tools/prepare_test40.py:72-89,147) and Builder/fix_binary (tools/prepare_test88.py:18,71).
le_cases() hand-assembles the Le Cases step and re-asserts each branch end is either the wanted fact or a positive-constant Absurd (tools/prepare_test44.py:11-23).

cut() re-derives the audit's node spec from the model (capacity row coefficients -7560/-30240/-120960, its matching packing row, 36 balance rows by name, D_n from the RHS) and then recursively expands the local options with EqPair forcing the unchosen options to zero (tools/prepare_test44.py:26-78).

block() emits the per-variable VarLower/VarUpper/Exact checks, the per-row dispatch (kept -> row_ref, removed -> Lin over other_rows, added -> cut) and the positional projection/inverse Exact runs (tools/prepare_test44.py:81-101).

main() writes 'RPA 3' + json.dumps(cert) into proof.rpa and a second copy of the claims into request.json, runs canonical/canonical/assemble/verify, then assembles and verifies five mutations (wrong_capacity, continuous_split, false_strictness, missing_middle, wrong_inverse) expecting INVALID (tools/prepare_test44.py:118-135).
friction: 72% of the RPA (2,372,342 B of 3,300,668 B) is one block's 37 nested Cases trees; the other two blocks cost 351,924 B and 317,268 B, so the certificate's size is driven entirely by the hand-expanded per-node case trees (cases/test44/proof.rpa).

request.json is 643,330 B but its compact claim content is 143,470 B: the inflation is three copies of the 4,161-pair identity projection printed as indented JSON, and the identical claims are written a second time inside proof.rpa (tools/prepare_test44.py:118).

Obligations have no address: the recorded middle-obligation attack has to delete checks by raw index (pop(2100) in block 1) and the counts 14,273/14,272/9,940 had to be hand-counted into metadata (tools/prepare_test44.py:130; cases/test44/preparation.json).

Points are bound to coordinates by name string: the integer point is derived with F(int('120960.000000' in v['name'])) and the strictness point is re-read from the 204,584 B audit-named witness.json (tools/prepare_test44.py:114-116).

The preparer consumes a per-case invented audit schema (101,730 B audit.json with removed_rows/added_rows/node/edges/demand) and re-derives every number with asserts because that schema is not part of any contract (tools/prepare_test44.py:44-47,88).
